artifacts.description: A per-decision record of appraisal outcome, retention binding, holds imposed and released, disposition authorisation and the evidence of destruction, transfer or migration. It states and evidences the disposition decision; it does not perform the disposition, which is executed by the carrying record model and the adopting Dimension's records authority.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Named {decision-master-identifier}-GOVDIS-{NNNN}, where the decision master identifier is the authoritative master-system identifier of the decision, GOVDIS is the fixed artefact-kind discriminator, and NNNN is a zero-padded monotonic sequence scoped to that decision master record and incremented for each disposition cycle. Sequence values are never reused and never derived from a date, retention year or schedule period.

functions.name: Frame the decision
functions.description: Establish the governed decision record: mint or bind its identifier, classify it against a decision type and jurisdictional profile, state the decision question and admissible answer space, record the triggering issue, objectives and critical success factors, and declare context dependencies and binding constraints.
inputs: Decision type code and jurisdictional profile identifier
Decision question text and admissible answer space
Objectives, critical success factors and impacted indicator references
Declared constraints, required input references and upstream decision references
outputs: Framed decision record carrying a resolvable identifier and version discriminator
Recorded decision question with its admissible answer space
Objective, constraint and dependency sets
Derived list of profile-required content elements
preconditions: An identifier is available from the identity priority order, master-system identifier first
The decision type and its bound profile are published by the profile custodian
effects: A uniquely identified decision record exists and is resolvable
Profile-required content elements are declared so later completeness checks are decidable
Framing content becomes the fixed reference against which the outcome statement is validated

functions.name: Register a candidate alternative
functions.description: Add a candidate alternative to the decision's alternative set with its own identifier, kind code and description, including registration of a no-action or business-as-usual baseline where the bound profile requires one.
inputs: Alternative kind code, including baseline or do-minimum where applicable
Variant-of reference where the alternative varies another
outputs: Registered alternative with its own identifier and registration ordinal
Updated alternative set for the decision
Baseline presence indicator for the bound profile
preconditions: The decision has been framed and its profile binding is known
The alternative is described in terms that the declared criteria can be applied to
effects: The alternative set is extended append-only; registered alternatives are never silently removed
Absence of a profile-required baseline becomes a detectable validation failure
Variants remain distinguishable from independently registered alternatives

functions.name: Declare the evaluation criteria and weights
functions.description: Record the criteria against which alternatives will be compared, each with its measure, scale, unit and preference direction, the separation of mandatory pass-or-fail criteria from compensatory ones, and the weighting scheme with its declared method or an explicit statement that no weighting is used.
inputs: Objectives and critical success factors from the framed decision
Candidate criteria with measures, scales and preference directions
Weighting method identifier and weight values where a weighting scheme applies
Monetisation convention where a criterion is expressed in monetary terms
outputs: Declared criterion set addressable by criterion identifier
Declared weighting scheme, or an explicit no-weighting statement
Classification of criteria as mandatory or compensatory
preconditions: Objectives and constraints have been framed
Each criterion is stated in terms that permit a result to be recorded against it
effects: Alternatives can be scored against a fixed and citable criterion set
Criteria that also act as eligibility filters are linked to the screening criteria
Weighting remains optional so that decisions without a weighting scheme are still complete

functions.name: Evaluate and compare the alternatives
functions.description: Record, as governed decision content, one evaluation round: eligibility screening results with reasons for exclusion, per-criterion results for admitted alternatives, any aggregation and ranking, sensitivity findings, and citations to evidence. Running an executable rule set or decision service to produce those results is outside this model.
inputs: Declared criterion set and screening criteria
Recorded results per alternative and criterion
Evidence item references supporting results or assumptions
outputs: Eligibility and exclusion results with a recorded reason for each exclusion
Alternative-by-criterion comparison matrix for the round
Aggregation, ranking and sensitivity findings
Result status markers for contested, provisional or bias-adjusted results
preconditions: At least one alternative is registered and the criterion set is declared
The evaluation round ordinal is available and has not been used
effects: A serially numbered, append-only evaluation round is recorded and never edited in place
Every excluded alternative carries an explicit recorded reason
Cited evidence is bound by identifier and role only; evidence appraisal, integrity and provenance stay with the evidence model
Execution traces of any external decision service are not captured here

functions.name: Record the selected decision outcome
functions.description: Record the selected alternative, the disposition, the explicit outcome statement answering the decision question, the declared effect onset and applicability, the factors expressly balanced, any explained divergence from the ranking, and the attached conditions, unresolved matters and stated consequences.
inputs: Selected alternative reference or declared variant description
Disposition code from the controlled list
Balanced factors and divergence explanation where the top-ranked alternative was not selected
Attached conditions, unresolved matters, accepted risks and reopening triggers
outputs: Outcome statement bound to the recorded decision question
Disposition code and selected alternative reference
Declared effect onset and applicability
Condition, reservation, consequence and raised-concern sets
preconditions: The alternative set contains the selected alternative or the alternative the selected variant derives from
Profile-required comparison and baseline content is present
The outcome statement falls within the recorded admissible answer space where one is declared
effects: The decision question has an explicit, immutable recorded answer; changing it requires a superseding decision that cites this one
Divergence from the evaluation ranking carries a recorded explanation where it occurs
Approval execution, publication, filing and enforcement of the outcome remain with the referenced activity, record and implementation models
Any monitoring or compliance work the conditions direct is executed and tracked by those models, not here

functions.name: Bind a reason to governed claims and evidence citations
functions.description: Attach claim references and evidence citation bindings to a reason or premise, recording citation type, locator and stance, and reporting any reference that does not resolve in its owning model.
inputs: evidence references with citation type, locator and stance
outputs: persisted binding set attached to the reason
resolution report listing resolved, superseded and dangling references
preconditions: The reason record exists and names the decision it explains by its master-system identifier
Citation types are drawn from a governed citation-typing vocabulary with a declared version
Referenced claim and evidence identifiers are resolvable in WM-KNW-007 and WM-KNW-008 respectively
effects: Creates or revises binding records only; never creates, alters, grades or retracts a referenced claim or evidence item
Records unresolvable references as declared gaps rather than substituting local content

functions.name: Assemble premises, inference and conclusion into an argument structure
functions.description: Record an argument as premises, a first-class inference element carrying a scheme reference, and a conclusion, together with asserted support and conflict relations and any critical-question responses.
inputs: argument element references with role codes
inference scheme reference and catalogue version
outputs: persisted argument structure record
argument structure export projection
preconditions: Every premise and conclusion slot references a governed claim or is explicitly marked as a local restatement
The scheme reference resolves in a declared catalogue, or the argument is flagged as informally schemed
effects: Records asserted inference and conflict only; performs no validity, soundness or entailment evaluation and issues no acceptability verdict
Leaves premise support status as asserted, without inferring support from the presence of a binding

functions.name: Re-check declared assumptions and sensitivity statements
functions.description: Compare declared assumptions, dependencies and sensitivity statements against the current state of the inputs and references they name, and annotate each with a status so that stale reasoning is visible.
inputs: assumption and dependency records with validity windows and defeat conditions
sensitivity variable references and recorded ranges
current resolution state of the referenced inputs
outputs: assumption status annotations
list of stale, defeated-by-declaration or unresolvable references
preconditions: Each assumption declares either a validity window, a defeat condition or an explicit unbounded marker
The referenced inputs expose a resolvable identity and revision
effects: Annotates existing records with a status and the time of the check; never edits the asserted assumption text
Does not execute the underlying analysis, does not re-run any model, does not enforce an outcome and does not change any decision state
Escalation, review scheduling and any consequent decision action are left to the `governance` split and the adopting Dimension

functions.name: Record an objection, counter-evidence or dissenting position
functions.description: Capture an objection or counter-argument against a named reason or inference, with its attribution, any counter-evidence binding, and an appended disposition where one has been stated.
inputs: objecting party reference and stated capacity
outputs: persisted objection record with attribution
dissenting or minority opinion artefact where a position is preserved separately
preconditions: The targeted reason, premise or inference exists
The objecting party is identified by reference to a record held outside this model
effects: Appends objection and disposition records; existing objections and dissent are never overwritten or removed
Applies argument-level defeated markings without altering the recorded outcome or any decision state
Adjudication authority, quorum and approval workflow remain with the `governance` split and are not exercised here

functions.name: Produce a bounded, audience-scoped explanation rendition
functions.description: Generate an explanation for a declared audience from a named rationale revision, attaching the omission set, the faithfulness assertion and the provenance of any machine-generated text.
inputs: rationale record set identifier and revision
declared audience and the entitlement or duty being answered
omission policy reference from the `governance` split
outputs: explanation rendition artefact with content digest
omission record stating what was withheld and on what ground
preconditions: The audience is declared and an omission policy reference resolves
The rationale revision to be rendered is resolvable and its provenance records are complete
Any machine-generated content carries its generating agent and version
effects: Emits a rendition linked to the rationale revision it renders, labelled where content was machine-generated
Creates no entitlement, discharges no regulatory duty and makes no representation that the reasoning is true, lawful or optimal
Is not an audit record: audit trails, access logging and disclosure approval remain with the `governance` split

functions.name: Register deciding authority and mandate binding
functions.description: Create or update the register entry that binds a deciding authority to a mandate instrument, its scope limits and its validity window, and attach that binding to a decision.
outputs: Authority register entry identifier
Authority binding attached to the decision
Lifecycle ledger entry
preconditions: The authority reference resolves in the party or governing-body register
The mandate instrument reference resolves and its validity window covers the decision event time
The caller holds the governance owner or decision authority role
effects: The decision carries a resolvable authority and mandate binding
Any subsequent authority claim is validated against this register entry
The registration is recorded as an append-only ledger entry with separated event and ingestion instants

functions.name: Record or revoke a delegation step
functions.description: Add a delegation or sub-delegation step with its ceiling, validity window and sub-delegation permission, or revoke an existing step and record the retrospectivity of the revocation.
inputs: Ceiling, validity window and sub-delegation flag
outputs: Delegation chain entry or revocation entry
Updated delegation chain for the decision
Lifecycle ledger entry
preconditions: The delegator holds a mandate or an upstream delegation that permits sub-delegation
The delegation window falls inside the upstream mandate window
effects: The competence chain from mandate holder to acting agent becomes traceable
Revocation marks the step closed without deleting it and records whether prior acts remain valid

functions.name: Declare an interest and record a recusal
functions.description: Capture a participant's declared interest, the determination made on it and any resulting recusal or mitigation action, together with its effective instant.
outputs: Interest declaration entry
Conflict determination entry
Recusal action with effective instant
preconditions: The participant appears on the decision's participant roster
The determining party is distinct from the declaring participant
effects: The participation record shows who was excluded and from which instant
Any recorded participation threshold figures are re-stated to reflect the recusal
Personal-data flags drive masking on later disclosure

functions.name: Attest satisfaction of the decision rule
functions.description: Record the presiding authority's own assertion that the applicable decision rule and participation threshold were satisfied, with the counted and required figures as asserted.
inputs: Decision rule code and prescribing provision reference
outputs: Quorum attestation entry
Participation mode recorded on the decision
Lifecycle ledger entry
preconditions: A participant roster exists for the decision
The attesting party holds a presiding or secretariat role for the proceeding
effects: The validity of the proceeding becomes inspectable as an attributed assertion
No threshold computation, evaluation or enforcement is performed or claimed by this model; the attestation records what the authority asserted

functions.name: Bind an approval or ratification act
functions.description: Attach an identifier-only reference to an external approval, ratification or endorsement activity record for a named governance stage and record the stage outcome.
inputs: Approval activity reference in the approval activity model
Stage outcome code and completion instant
outputs: Approval stage entry
Updated pipeline completeness state
Lifecycle ledger entry
preconditions: The referenced approval activity identifier resolves in the approval activity model
The stage is defined in the applicable procedure
effects: The decision's approval pipeline becomes traceable to external evidence
Approval execution, assignment and completion semantics remain owned by the referenced activity model

functions.name: Apply a governed status transition
functions.description: Move the decision from one governed status to another — including to effective, conditional, suspended, superseded, revoked, expired or reopened — recording the acting authority, ground, effective instant and any successor reference.
inputs: Acting authority reference and ground code
Successor or superseding version reference where applicable
outputs: Status transition entry
Updated current status
Lifecycle ledger entry
preconditions: The transition is permitted from the current status by the governed transition table
The acting authority is competent for that transition
No unreleased legal hold blocks a transition to a disposition-bearing state
effects: The decision's reliability at a given instant becomes determinable
Superseded versions remain retrievable; no approved version is mutated by a transition

functions.name: Open a review, appeal or reopening
functions.description: Open a review, appeal or reconsideration against the decision, recording the trigger or appellant, the competent forum, the applicable window and the status held while the matter is open.
outputs: Review or appeal entry with its due and expiry instants
Status entry reflecting the open matter
Lifecycle ledger entry
preconditions: The requesting party falls within an eligible appellant class for the tier
The request instant falls inside the applicable window
effects: The reconsideration obligation becomes trackable and time-bounded
The original version remains retrievable in its approved form while the matter is open

functions.name: Classify access and schedule disclosure
functions.description: Set or revise the access class for each addressed part of the decision, record the exemption grounds and redaction profile, and set embargo and proactive-publication instants.
inputs: Access class codes and classifying authority reference
Exemption ground codes and provision references
Embargo end instant and publication channel reference
outputs: Access and disclosure schedule version
Discoverable metadata set
Lifecycle ledger entry
preconditions: The classifying authority holds the release or classification role
Any exemption ground cites a resolvable provision reference
effects: Downstream systems obtain a declarative instruction for release and redaction
Enforcement of the classification is performed by the access-control system, not by this model

functions.name: Impose or release a legal hold
functions.description: Record the imposition or release of a legal hold or disposition freeze over the decision record, with the imposing authority, ground, scope and instants.
outputs: Hold entry with updated hold state
Suspension flag on pending disposition actions
Lifecycle ledger entry
preconditions: The imposing party holds legal or records authority in the adopting Dimension
A release names the hold entry it releases
effects: All disposition actions are blocked while any hold is in force
Hold history remains retrievable after release for defensibility

functions.name: Request disposition or tombstoning
functions.description: Request a disposition outcome for the decision record — retain, destroy, transfer, migrate or tombstone — with its authorisation, and record the evidence returned by the executing custodian.
inputs: Retention schedule reference and trigger instant
Disposition evidence reference returned by the executor
outputs: Disposition record entry
Tombstone record where content is removed
Lifecycle ledger entry
preconditions: The retention period has elapsed from the recorded trigger instant
No hold is in force
An appraisal outcome exists for records of potential permanent value
effects: Execution is performed by the carrying record model and the adopting Dimension's records authority, not here
Identity, authority, status and disposition facts survive in the tombstone unless an authorised erasure rule requires their removal

functions.name: Seal a version and verify its integrity
functions.description: Compute and store the digest over the declared canonical form of a governed version, attach any signature or timestamp-token reference, and later verify a retrieved projection against the stored digest.
inputs: Version identifier and canonical form declaration
Signature or timestamp-token reference where available
outputs: Digest value bound to the version
Verification outcome entry
Lifecycle ledger entry
preconditions: The canonicalization rules for the projection are declared
The sealing agent is identified
effects: Integrity of a version becomes independently checkable
A failed verification quarantines the projection and raises a notification; the sealed version is never corrected in place
Audit-record generation and retention remain with the referenced audit system

composition.purpose: Register the decision under its knowledge parent. Generic assertion identity, truth-value, endorsement and claim-conflict machinery stay with the parent; this model adds only decision-specific specialisation, namely the alternative set, criteria, evaluation and disposition.

Bind evidence cited in support of an evaluation result or a declared assumption, carrying the evidence identifier and the role of the citation. Evidence appraisal, sufficiency, integrity and chain of custody remain with the target and are never reproduced here.

Reference the activity that produced and approved the decision, so that participants, deliberation, quorum and approval execution can be resolved. This model carries the reference and any decision-specific binding parameters only; the activity's lifecycle and execution semantics stay with the target.

Reference the record that expresses, files or publishes this decision content, following the Work and Expression separation from Manifestation and Item. Rendering, formatting, publication, preservation and record-level retention execution stay with the target.

Where the decision is judicial, align the outcome content to the judgment's decision section and its background and motivation structure. The judgment's binding legal force, enforceability and citation regime remain with the target; alignment asserts no conformance.

Carry the back-reference from a decision to the change request it resolves, matching the incoming relation in the ledger. The request's own lifecycle, prioritisation and the implementation, monitoring and compliance work that follows the decision belong to the target.

composition.target: OMG Decision Model and Notation (DMN) version 1.5
composition.purpose: Align framing vocabulary to DMN element names for interchange: question, allowedAnswers, informationRequirement, knowledgeRequirement, supportedObjective, impactedPerformanceIndicator and decision table hitPolicy. Alignment only; no conformance is claimed, DMN identifiers are document-scoped and do not satisfy the identity priority, and execution of DMN decision logic stays with a decision service.

composition.target: Jurisdictional appraisal and record-of-decision profiles (HM Treasury Green Book, US NEPA record-of-decision pattern)
composition.purpose: Bind an optional jurisdictional profile that adds required content elements, such as a mandatory business-as-usual baseline, recorded reasons for eliminating alternatives, identification of a preferable alternative and declared mitigation conditions. Profiles are opt-in per decision type; none is a global default and the NEPA pattern is cited as historical.

Registry-declared parent. Decision rationale is a specialisation of governed assertion content: premises and conclusions are references to claims that WM-KNW-007 identifies, versions and verifies. This model adds only the argument role a claim occupies, the version pinned at reasoning time and any marked local restatement; it never issues claim identity, changes claim wording or records claim verification status.

Decision rationale cites evidence. This model carries the evidence reference, the citation type, the locator into the cited resource, the citation stance and the decision-local appraisal of how far the evidence bears on this decision. Evidence identity, acquisition, chain of custody, intrinsic certainty grading and evidence retention remain in WM-KNW-008 and are carried by reference; a referenced certainty grade is read and reproduced unchanged with its read time, never recomputed here.

Incoming registry-declared relation: a change request is resolved by a decision and references the decision record. This model exposes stable rationale identifiers so that such a reference can resolve, and nothing more. Change-request intake, triage, workflow and closure are owned by WM-ACT-032, and no function here advances or evaluates a change request.

composition.target: OMG Structured Assurance Case Metamodel (SACM) 2.3, Argumentation package
composition.purpose: Alignment target for argument structure: claims, argument reasoning, asserted inference, asserted evidence and counter-argument or counter-evidence links. Mapping is asserted at the level of element roles only; no conformance is claimed and the alignment does not import SACM's assurance-case lifecycle or its notation.

Alignment target for representing inference, conflict and preference as first-class nodes and for scheme forms carrying premises, conclusions, exceptions and presumptions. Used to justify first-class inference elements and scheme references; AIF's dialogue extensions are outside this model's scope.

Alignment target for reasoning provenance: attribution of rationale to a person or software agent, association with a generating activity, derivation from prior rationale, and generation time. Adopting the vocabulary does not transfer any responsibility, access or retention semantics to this model.

Alignment target for the citation-type vocabulary used in evidence bindings, including cited as evidence, cited as authority, supports, disagrees with and refutes. Citation types characterise the citing act only and are never interpreted as evidential weight or quality grades.

Alignment target for locators that pinpoint the cited part of a resource using quotation, position or fragment selectors, and for creator, created, generator and generated provenance on annotations. Used to reference precisely without copying cited content into this model.

composition.target: Goal Structuring Notation Community Standard, Version 3
composition.purpose: Alignment target for separating assumption from supported goal, justification from claim, and solution as a reference to evidence, and for the dialectic notions of challenge and defeated as argument-level annotations. No claim is made that a rationale record constitutes a GSN-conformant assurance case.

composition.target: GRADE certainty-of-evidence framework as rendered in the ACIP GRADE Handbook
composition.purpose: Alignment target for carrying a referenced certainty grade and for distinguishing the grading of a body of evidence from a decision-local appraisal. Grading domains, methodology and the act of grading remain with the evidence model; this model reproduces the grade with its framework identifier and read time.

Specialises the parent knowledge-assertion model for the decision subject by adding decision-specific mandate, participation, approval and validity-state governance. Generic assertion identity, claim typing and evidential binding machinery stay in the parent and are not restated here.

Carries identifier-only references from decision content provenance to evidence records. Evidence identity, appraisal, quality grading and chain-of-custody semantics remain in the target; rationale-level evidence binding is owned by the reasoning area of this model.

Binds each approval, ratification or endorsement stage to the external activity record that evidences it. This model stores the binding identifier, stage code and outcome; activity initiation, assignment, execution and completion remain owned by the target.

Names the record that carries the decision and the authority that executes retention, transfer and destruction. This model states the retention binding, hold state, disposition authorisation and tombstone content; repository placement and physical execution remain owned by the target.
References a judicial or tribunal judgment that determines an appeal against the decision. Court composition, pleadings, orders, remedies and judicial reasoning are not modelled here.

Inbound relation: a change request is resolved by a decision. This model retains only the resolved change-request identifier and the resolution instant; change-request intake, triage, states and closure remain owned by the source model.

A decision may be constrained by, or may establish, a policy or executable rule. Only the reference, its binding role and any decision-specific parameters are held here; rule authoring, runtime evaluation, obligation discharge and enforcement remain external and are never inferred from the reference.

composition.target: ISO 15489-1:2016 records management concepts and principles
composition.purpose: Aligns authoritativeness, metadata, assigned responsibilities, records controls and appraisal-driven disposition. Alignment only: no conformance is claimed, since conformance depends on the adopting Dimension's records system and policy.

Maps attribution, qualified association with roles, delegation, revision, derivation and invalidation onto local provenance and delegation structures for interchange. Local semantics prevail where they diverge.

Maps in-force status, consolidation, amendment and repeal relations and authority attribution onto the local status and supersession model where the decision is a normative instrument. The ELI identifier, when assigned, ranks as a governed global identifier and does not displace the master-system identifier.

composition.target: W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model v2.0
composition.purpose: Maps issuer attribution, validity windows and revocation or suspension status onto the local authority and status model where a decision is projected as a verifiable credential. Credential formats and proof mechanisms remain a projection concern.

composition.target: OASIS Akoma Ntoso v1.0 Part 1 XML Vocabulary
composition.purpose: Maps FRBR-style work, expression, manifestation and item identification, lifecycle events, temporal data and top-level person, role and organisation references onto local version identity and participation structures for legislative and deliberative contexts.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension must name one accountable decision-governance owner package and its owning organisational unit before any governance record is created; unowned governance records are invalid.

The owner package must publish the decision-rights or mandate catalogue it operates, the status vocabulary and permitted transitions, and the retention schedule authority under which it disposes of decision records.

The owner package must declare the jurisdictional profiles in force — at minimum the access-to-documents regime, the data-protection regime and any sector records legislation — and the local overrides each imposes on the default rules in this model.

The owner package must nominate a custodian for every stored projection and a reviewer or review forum for every decision class subject to periodic review, and must keep those nominations current through the role handover function.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use one stable, dereferenceable namespace owned by the adopting Dimension, shaped as {dimension-base-iri}/decision-governance/{local-id}, where {local-id} is the master identifier or the Dimension-assigned ULID. Never encode a date, a status, an access class or an organisational unit into the namespace path, because all four change while identity must not. Where a governed global identifier such as an ELI-style legal identifier exists it is recorded as an alias and may be minted in its own namespace, but it never replaces the master identifier in the local namespace. Artefact-kind discriminators (GOVLED, GOVACC, GOVDIS) are part of the artefact name, not of the namespace.
registry_links: Vercy registry entry vr.wm-knw-010 for model identity, entry kind, status and review state
planning/VERCY-MODEL-RELATIONS.csv for the authoritative relation ledger governing composition and ownership boundaries
The adopting Dimension's decision authority and delegation register, resolved through dr-gov-art-authority-register
The adopting Dimension's retention schedule register and its issuing records authority

canonicalization_rules: Serialize with deterministic member ordering and a declared character encoding; the digest in the integrity rule is computed over this canonical form and the canonical form must be named alongside the digest.

Normalise every timestamp to RFC 3339 with explicit seconds and an explicit offset or Z, and retain the originally submitted offset as a separate field so that local civil time is not lost by normalisation.
Represent identifiers verbatim as issued by their master system, including case; do not case-fold, trim or re-pad a master identifier, and record any locally applied alias separately.
Store codes as code plus code-system reference; never store a display label as the value. Absent and empty are distinct: an absent field means not stated, an empty collection means stated as none.
patch_rules: The lifecycle ledger is append-only. Entries are never edited or removed; a correction is a new entry that references the entry it corrects and states the reason.

An approved or effective version is immutable. Substantive change is expressed by issuing a new version with a supersession reference, never by mutating the prior version; editorial correction to an approved version requires an erratum entry citing the authorising party.
Status changes only through the governed transition function, which validates the transition against the declared transition table and records acting authority, ground and effective instant.
Every patch carries the acting agent, the reason code, and both the event instant and the ingestion instant; a patch missing any of these is rejected.
Access classification and retention bindings are versioned, not overwritten: a reissued access schedule or disposition record increments its own zero-padded sequence and retains its predecessor.
compatibility_rules: Adding an optional data element, an optional question or a new alignment is a minor, backward-compatible change.
Removing or narrowing a status value, an access class, a role or a code system, or making an optional element required, is breaking and requires a new major model version and a migration note.

Changing an alignment mapping is non-breaking where local semantics are unchanged; the alignment record must state the source version it maps to so that a target standard's revision does not silently alter local meaning.
Versioning applies to the model and to individual decision records independently: a model version change never rewrites the version identifiers of existing decision records.
Consumers must ignore unknown members rather than fail, but must not infer a default for an absent required element.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier: the identifier issued by the system of record for the decision — typically the deciding body's decision or minute register number — used verbatim as the decision master identifier and never re-minted locally.

Governed global identifier or IRI assigned by a recognised registry, such as an ELI-style legal identifier or another registry-governed IRI, used when no master-system identifier exists or recorded as an alias when one does.

UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension, flagged as Dimension-assigned, used only when neither of the above exists; if a master identifier is later issued it is adopted as primary while the Dimension-assigned identifier is retained permanently as an alias.
A date, a meeting name, a title, an agenda item number, a file path or a bare sequence is never an identifier and must not be used as one, alone or in combination.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All timestamps are RFC 3339 date-time values that include explicit seconds and an explicit UTC offset or the Z designator; a bare date, a date-time without seconds, and a date-time with no offset are all rejected. The offset -00:00 is used only where the instant in UTC is known but the local offset genuinely is not. Event time (when the governance act occurred, such as the decision being taken or a hold being imposed), observation time (when the fact was witnessed, attested or reported by a named party) and ingestion time (when the Vercy record captured it) are stored in separate fields and are never merged, back-filled from each other, or defaulted to the current clock; where a fact has only one meaningful time axis, the unused axes are left absent rather than duplicated.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Every serial governance artefact is named {decision-master-identifier}-{artefact-kind}-{NNNN}: the decision master identifier resolved by the identity priority above, a fixed artefact-kind discriminator (GOVLED for the lifecycle and change ledger, GOVACC for the access and disclosure schedule, GOVDIS for the review, hold and disposition record), and NNNN, a zero-padded monotonic sequence whose scope is explicitly the decision master record. Sequences start at 0001, are never reused after supersession or deletion, and are never derived from a date, timestamp, retention year, review cycle or period label. A gap in a sequence must be explained by a lifecycle ledger entry. Non-serial artefacts, such as the authority and delegation register, take their identity from the identity priority instead and are keyed by authority plus mandate instrument.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Each governed version and each serial artefact version records a named digest algorithm, the digest value computed over the declared canonical form, the sealing agent and the sealing instant, plus any signature, seal or timestamp-token reference evidencing non-repudiation. Verification compares a retrieved projection against the stored digest and writes a verification outcome entry; a failure quarantines the projection and raises a notification, and the sealed version is never corrected in place. Vercy stores integrity values and references only: generating, protecting, reviewing and retaining audit trails, and enforcing any control derived from them, belong to the referenced records and audit systems.

policies: Authority before content: no decision record may reach an approved or effective status without a resolvable deciding authority and mandate binding whose validity window covers the decision event time.

Reference, do not reproduce: approval activities, carrying records, legal judgments, claims, evidence, policies and executable rules are held as identifiers with a binding role and decision-specific parameters only; their internal structures, lifecycles and operational functions are never mirrored here.

No local evaluation or enforcement: this model records assertions, classifications and instructions. Threshold evaluation, access enforcement, rule execution, obligation discharge and audit-trail generation are performed by external systems, and referencing such a system never transfers its semantics to this model.

Immutability after approval: approved and effective versions are immutable; change is expressed through new versions, supersession and append-only ledger entries, so that what was relied upon at a past instant remains reconstructable.

Tombstone-first disposition: content is superseded or tombstoned rather than erased unless an authorised erasure rule applies, and identity, authority, status and disposition facts survive every disposition that is not itself an authorised erasure of those facts.

Declared profiles, no global claims: jurisdiction-specific access, integrity and retention duties are recorded as named profiles or alignments; the model never asserts conformance to a standard or a legal regime without evidence recorded in the adopting Dimension.

read: Read is governed by the access classification held for each addressed part; the outcome, the rationale reference set and the governance metadata may carry different classes and are evaluated separately.

Register-level metadata declared in the discoverable metadata set — master identifier, subject reference, deciding authority and decision date — remains discoverable to authenticated readers even where content is withheld, unless a sensitive-item rule restricts the existence of the item itself.

Where an exemption covers only part of a record, readers receive the parts not covered, produced through the declared redaction profile; a partial release is recorded as a disclosure event in the lifecycle ledger.
Reads resolve references without dereferencing target-model content: a reader receives approval, evidence, record and judgment identifiers, not copies of those records.
Point-in-time reads must be answerable: given an instant, the reader can determine which version was authoritative and which status applied.
create: Only a party holding the governance owner or decision authority role may create a governance record, and creation must bind the decision master identifier, the deciding authority and the mandate reference.
Creation records the ingestion instant separately from the decision event instant, and a draft record must not carry an effective status or an effective instant.
A newly created record with no master-system identifier is minted a Dimension-assigned ULID that is flagged as such and retained as an alias if a master identifier later appears.
Creation opens the lifecycle ledger for the decision with an initial entry naming the creating agent, the capture mode and the source system where the record was imported or migrated.
update: Governance metadata on a draft may be updated in place; once a version is approved or effective it is immutable and change proceeds by new version and supersession reference.
Every update writes an append-only lifecycle ledger entry with acting agent, reason code, significance code and the separated event and ingestion instants; silent edits are rejected.
Status changes only through the governed transition function and only where the transition is permitted from the current status and the acting authority is competent for it.
Corrections to approved content are recorded as errata that cite the authorising party and leave the corrected version retrievable in its original sealed form.
No update may weaken an access classification or shorten a retention binding without a recorded authorisation from the classifying or records authority.
delete: Deletion is tombstone-first and supersession-first: superseding, revoking or expiring a decision never removes it, and content removal requires a disposition authorisation recorded in dr-gov-art-disposition-record.
Disposition is blocked while any legal hold or disposition freeze is in force, and while a review, appeal or reconsideration is open against the decision.

When an authorised disposition removes content, the surviving tombstone retains the decision master identifier and any aliases, the version identifier, the deciding authority reference, the status at disposition, the disposition action code, the disposition authorisation reference and the disposition instant, together with the lifecycle ledger entries that evidence the disposition.

Execution of destruction, transfer or migration is not performed by this model: it is owned by the carrying record model WM-REC-010 and the adopting Dimension's records authority operating under its published retention schedule, and this model records only the authorisation, the request and the evidence returned.

An authorised erasure rule — for example a data-protection erasure duty, subject to its own statutory exceptions for legal obligations, public-interest tasks, archiving and the defence of legal claims — may require removal of identifying content from the tombstone itself; where it applies, the erasure authorisation reference, its legal basis and the resulting reduced tombstone are recorded, and the surviving audit and integrity facts held by the external audit system are not deleted by this model.

Deletion of an entire lifecycle ledger, access schedule or disposition record is never permitted while the decision record exists; these artefacts are disposed of only as part of the decision's own authorised disposition.

roles.name: Decision authority
responsibilities: Take the decision within the mandate and record the authority and mandate binding
Attest satisfaction of the applicable decision rule and participation threshold
Authorise status transitions such as suspension, revocation and reopening
Determine whether a declared interest is disqualifying where the rules assign that determination to the chair or presiding office

roles.name: Governance owner
responsibilities: Own the decision record as a governed asset and account for its completeness
Maintain the authority and delegation register entries relied on by the decision
Approve role handovers and nominate custodians and reviewers
Declare the jurisdictional profiles applied to the record

roles.name: Records steward
responsibilities: Maintain the accuracy of governance metadata, including status, effective dating and version chain
Write and quality-check lifecycle ledger entries and errata
Bind the record to the correct retention schedule item and trigger
Prepare disposition requests and record the evidence returned

roles.name: Custodian
responsibilities: Hold and protect a stored projection of the record
Compute and store digests over the declared canonical form and report verification outcomes
Execute or relay disposition instructions to the executing records authority
Preserve tombstones and integrity references after content removal

roles.name: Reviewer or appeal forum
responsibilities: Conduct scheduled and triggered reviews by the recorded due instant
Receive appeals and reconsideration requests within the applicable window
Record the review outcome and its relation to the original decision without overwriting it
Refer matters to a judicial forum where the escalation tier requires it

roles.name: Access and disclosure authority
responsibilities: Set and revise access classifications and exemption grounds
Approve partial access and the redaction profile applied
Release the decision proactively when an embargo lapses
Apply personal-data minimisation before any disclosure

access.default_rule: Deny by default at finding and artefact scope. A reader obtains content only where an access class explicitly grants it for the addressed part; register-level metadata in the declared discoverable set is available to authenticated readers unless a sensitive-item rule restricts even the existence of the record. Enforcement is performed by the adopting Dimension's access-control system; this model supplies the classification and the disclosure instruction only.
exceptions: Proactive publication: once an embargo lapses and no hold or open appeal blocks release, the decision is published through the recorded channel by the named release authority.

Statutory access request: a request under an access-to-documents regime is answered by releasing the parts not covered by an exemption, applying the redaction profile, and giving written reasons for any refusal together with the available remedies.

Sensitive-item handling: items classified as sensitive are handled only by authorised personnel and are released only with the originating authority's consent, and their register references are worded so as not to disclose the protected content.
Legal hold and discovery access: a party conducting a hold or discovery obtains access for that purpose under a recorded authorisation, without altering the record's classification.

Emergency break-glass: an urgent operational need may be met by a time-boxed override that is recorded with the requester, the justification and the expiry instant, and that requires post-hoc ratification by the access and disclosure authority.
audit_requirements: Every access decision records the requester, the addressed scope, whether access was granted, refused or partial, and the exemption ground where refused or redacted.
Every break-glass override records its justification, its expiry instant and the outcome of its post-hoc ratification.
Disclosure events, embargo lapses and classification changes are written to the lifecycle ledger with separated event and ingestion instants.

Audit records themselves are generated, protected and retained by the external audit system identified in the audit trail reference; this model retains only the correlation identifier and a coverage note stating which governance acts are expected to appear there.

read_order: AGENTS.md first, to obtain Name, Type and the four URLs before touching any record
Specification URL, to load scope, boundaries, status vocabulary and permitted transitions
Relation ledger URL, to confirm which concepts are owned here and which belong to referenced models
Storage type URL, to learn the projection in use and its canonical form, whether that is a document store, a graph, a repository or a collection
Interface URL, to learn how identifiers resolve and how reads are scoped by access class
Processes URL, to learn the governed functions, their preconditions and the roles competent to invoke them
Only then read or write records, resolving the decision master identifier before any artefact name is constructed

coverage.claim: Audited as a bounded reviewable single-provider draft: 33 sources, 9 bundles, 18 layers, 39 findings, 175 questions across 27 question kinds, 14 artefacts and 21 functions, routed across decision core, rationale and governance with one designated owner per checklist dimension. Coverage is claimed only against that routed checklist, the two registered ledger relations and the declared jurisdictional profiles; it is not universal. Three dimensions are self-declared gaps (causal and counterfactual rationale, reason weighting and aggregation semantics, participation and conflict-of-interest structure), one is not-applicable by boundary, and twenty known omissions plus sixteen regional assumptions remain open. No independent second-provider corroboration exists, and no source URL or version pin was re-resolved in this no-tools audit. No contradiction found in this audit prevents publication of a reviewable draft carrying the holds below.

checklist.notes: Master-system identifier first, then a governed global identifier, then a Dimension-minted UUID or ULID; version discriminator, supersession links and labelled non-authoritative alternate identifiers. DMN's tDMNElement identifier is an xsd:ID scoped to one interchange document and is treated as an alignment only, never as a source of stable identity.

Typed references for the triggering issue, sub-decisions, upstream decisions, required inputs, knowledge sources, affected subjects, addressed and raised concerns, superseded decisions and follow-on decisions. Each outbound link is a reference or alignment, never an embedded copy.

Append-only registration of alternatives with kind codes, variant links and a profile-conditional no-action or business-as-usual baseline, grounded in the Green Book 2026 mandatory benchmark and the 2024 CFR edition of 40 CFR 1502.14(c).

Criteria with definition, measure, scale, unit and preference direction; mandatory versus compensatory classification; optional weights with a declared method. Named MCDA methods and their axioms remain optional external bindings.

Per-criterion results, aggregation, ranking and sensitivity recorded as serially numbered append-only rounds, with a comparison-matrix artefact. Runtime execution of any decision service that produced the numbers is explicitly excluded.

Selected alternative, disposition code, immutable outcome statement, balanced factors, divergence explanation and separately identified preferable alternative, following the record-of-decision content pattern without owning the published record.

Constraint limits, criterion measures, scales, units, preference directions, scores, aggregates and monetisation basis are explicit; quantities carry units and monetised values carry a currency and price base.

Decision type binds a profile that declares required content elements and validation rules. No global default profile is asserted, and profiles are modelled as an opt-in MIX-IN rather than as built-in requirements.

Confidence qualifiers carry a named scale, an explicit subject (evidence, inference or outcome) and stated knowledge limits, and are kept inline with what they qualify so a figure cannot circulate without its scale.

Counter-arguments, counter-evidence, objection attribution, appended dispositions, argument-level defeated markings and separately attributed minority opinions are modelled and protected from overwrite, with adjudication authority left to governance.

Every rendition carries the rendered rationale revision, derivation method, omission record and a non-suppressible generated-content label, matching the requirement that an explanation reflect the process that produced the output rather than a plausible reconstruction.

Modelled only as assertion records with a strength qualifier, cited basis and competing-explanation note. No consulted primary source defines a normative structure for counterfactual rationale, so this finding is marked as a gap rather than presented as canonical, and the model never upgrades an association to an asserted cause.

Asserted reason weights and decision-local evidential weights are carried with a mandatory scale reference, but no consulted primary source supplies a governed weighting or aggregation semantics. Weights are therefore recorded as asserted values only and must not be summed, compared across decisions or treated as calibrated.

A controlled status vocabulary covers draft, submitted, approved, effective, conditional, suspended, superseded, revoked, expired and reopened with a transition table, competent authorities and separated approval, publication and effective instants. RFC 2026 supplies staged maturity, retirement and appeal precedent; ELI supplies in-force, consolidation and repeal relations.

All instants are RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; event, observation and ingestion times are separate fields; validity windows, embargo lapse, appeal windows and retention triggers are modelled explicitly. Retrospective effect is flagged where the effective instant precedes approval.

Attribution, derivation, attestation and capture mode align to PROV-O qualified patterns; the append-only ledger records acting agent, reason and authority for every governance act. Cited claims and evidence are identifier-only references.

Owner, steward, custodian and reviewer are distinguished, with handover events and residual accountability, and separated from the deciding authority that owns the substance. Six service-layer roles carry explicit responsibilities.

Quorum and decision-rule satisfaction is recorded as an attributed assertion by the presiding authority rather than computed here; integrity verification produces an outcome entry without mutating the sealed version; approval defects have codes and remediation paths.

Deny by default at all four scopes, per-part classification, exemption grounds with provision references, partial access by redaction, discoverable register metadata and five named exceptions including a ratified break-glass override. Enforcement is explicitly external.

Retention schedule binding with an explicit start trigger, legal hold blocking disposition, tombstone-first deletion with an enumerated surviving field set, named executing owner (WM-REC-010 and the Dimension records authority), archival transfer for permanent-value records, and an authorised-erasure path with its statutory exceptions.

Six alignments recorded as alignments only — ISO 15489-1, PROV-O, ELI 1.5, VC Data Model 2.0, Akoma Ntoso and NARA's requirement categories — each stating that local semantics prevail on divergence and that no conformance is claimed.

Mandate instrument, scope limits, validity window, succession and ultra vires handling are modelled, with the authority register as the resolution point. Grounded in ISO 15489-1 assigned responsibilities, ELI responsibility_of_agent and passed_by, and the Council's Rules of Procedure.

Participation mode, proxy representation and quorum attestation are grounded in Council Decision 2009/937/EU, which is jurisdiction-specific. No cross-domain primary standard was found for a conflict-of-interest register schema or for recusal effects on thresholds; the OECD conflict-of-interest guidance could not be retrieved during this pass, so this structure is marked as a gap rather than presented as canonical.

Digest algorithm and value over a declared canonical form, sealing agent, signature or timestamp-token reference, quarantine-on-failure and an external audit correlation identifier. Audit generation, protection and retention are stated as externally owned in line with the NIST control families.

Held only as identifier-only follow-up obligation references with the owning model named. Implementation progress, delivery data and outcome measurement are outside this model's boundary by design and no local structure is offered for them.

known_omissions: Group aggregation and voting rules, including tie-breaking and dissent recording, which the sources consulted do not settle.
Probabilistic decision structures such as decision trees, influence diagrams and expected-utility calculations, treated as optional method bindings.
Named multi-criteria methods and their axioms, including AHP, ELECTRE, PROMETHEE and TOPSIS.
Domain rule content such as clinical protocols, credit scorecards, procurement award formulas and sentencing guidelines.
Appraisal cost conventions such as discount rate, price base and currency, which are jurisdiction-specific and change independently of this model.
Machine-learning model cards or feature attributions for automated decisions, which belong to a model-governance sibling rather than to decision content.
No normative structure for counterfactual or causal rationale was found in any consulted primary source; the corresponding finding is flagged as a gap and carries assertions only.
Deliberation and dialogue modelling — turn taking, protocol state, quorum and voting mechanics — is omitted; AIF dialogue extensions and inference-anchoring approaches were not adopted.

Formal defeasible-reasoning semantics (abstract argumentation frameworks, structured argumentation calculi) are not adopted; conflict and defeat are recorded as asserted annotations with no acceptability computation.

Domain-specific reason taxonomies — legal grounds of decision, clinical reasoning categories, procurement justification codes — are left to the adopting Dimension's published vocabulary rather than enumerated here.
Multilingual equivalence between language versions of a stated reason is not modelled beyond retaining the original language tag and forbidding silent translation.

Normative clauses of ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010-2022 and ISO/IEC/IEEE 15026-2 on rationale and assurance cases are paywalled and were not consulted; only publicly available scope text was used, so architecture-description rationale requirements are not reflected in detail.
Quantitative confidence calibration methods and the mapping between verbal qualifiers and numeric ranges are required to be published but no default mapping is supplied.

No controlled vocabulary is fixed for decision rules, recusal actions or reopening grounds; the adopting Dimension must publish one, and the codes here are placeholders bound to a code-system reference.

ISO 16175-1:2020 and the ISO 23081 metadata-for-records series were not directly consulted because their texts are paywalled; the records-metadata entity model, including an explicit mandate entity, is therefore inferred from ISO 15489-1 and NARA rather than from the most specific standard available.

The OECD guidance on managing conflict of interest in the public service could not be retrieved during this pass, so conflict-of-interest structure rests on a single EU procedural instrument and a data-protection instrument.
No structure is offered for meeting minutes or proceedings as such; where minutes exist they are referenced, and the model does not attempt to be a substitute account of a sitting.
Voting tallies are not modelled beyond an attested counted-and-required pair, because the dissent and objection content is owned by the reasoning area and a full ballot structure would duplicate it.
Cost, effort and resourcing consequences of a decision are not modelled at all; they belong to planning and financial models outside this boundary.
Cryptographic scheme profiles, key management and trust anchors are referenced but not specified; they belong to the adopting Dimension's security model.
conflicts: OMG DMN models a reusable decision definition inside a decision requirements graph, whereas WM-KNW-010 governs an instance-level decision taken on a specific occasion. DMN carries no version attribute on Decision and its identifier is an xsd:ID scoped to one interchange document, so DMN identifiers cannot satisfy the Vercy identity priority. Recorded as an alignment conflict, not resolved by adopting DMN identity.

DMN's Decision element has no representation for alternatives, criteria, weights, rationale or disposition; it carries question, allowedAnswers, requirement links and an expression. DMN therefore supports the framing findings but cannot support the alternatives, evaluation or outcome findings, which is why those are grounded in appraisal and decision-analysis sources instead.

The no action alternative requirement in 40 CFR 1502.14(c) and the record-of-decision content in 40 CFR 1505.2 are cited from the 2024 CFR annual edition. CEQ removed 40 CFR parts 1500 to 1508 by interim final rule at 90 FR 10610, published 25 February 2025 and effective 11 April 2025, directing agencies to rely on their own procedures. These are therefore cited as a historical normative content pattern, not as currently binding government-wide requirements.

HM Treasury's supplementary guidance restricts multi-criteria decision analysis to longlist appraisal and warns that it is resource-intensive and needs specialist practitioners, which conflicts with widespread practice of weighted scoring at shortlist stage. Weights are consequently modelled as optional and never as a completeness requirement.

GDPR Article 22 uses decision in a legal-effects sense that coincides with neither DMN's technical decision node nor ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010's architecture decision. The model does not reconcile these senses; it makes decision type and jurisdictional profile explicit so the intended sense is always recoverable.

ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 treats architecture rationale as a first-class element distinct from the decision, while appraisal guidance folds justification into the appraisal record itself. This model follows 42010 and keeps rationale separate, which means a Green Book style appraisal summary maps across two areas of WM-KNW-010 rather than one.

Structured-argument metamodels and the Argument Interchange Format both make inference and conflict first-class but with different primitives — asserted inference and evidence links with counter flags versus rule-application, conflict-application and preference-application nodes — and no normative crosswalk between them exists. This model records element roles abstractly and asserts only role-level alignment.

Goal Structuring Notation's Justification, the assurance metamodel's ArgumentReasoning and the Argument Interchange Format's rule-application node are frequently treated as equivalent in practice but are not defined equivalently; conflating them would silently change what is being asserted.

Citation typing is rhetorical and bibliographic while certainty-of-evidence grading is methodological. A citation type such as 'cites as evidence' carries no quality claim, yet tooling routinely presents the two together; this model forbids reading a citation type as a grade.

Web Annotation motivation values do not include an evidential-citation motivation, so citation type must come from a separate citation vocabulary while locators come from the annotation model; the two vocabularies are combined without a published joint profile.

Explainability guidance requires explanations to be accurate to the generating process, while regulation frames the explanation as an entitlement of an affected person expressed in accessible terms. These pull in different directions for technical decisions, and the model resolves it by requiring an explicit omission record rather than by preferring one over the other.

Records doctrine treats a captured record as fixed, while ELI and Akoma Ntoso treat a legal text as an expression that is consolidated and versioned over time. Resolved here by making versions immutable once approved and expressing all change as new versions with supersession links, so both readings hold, but adopters projecting to a records system that forbids multiple live expressions will need a profile.

A data-protection erasure duty can require removal of identifying content that a retention schedule and a legal hold require to be kept. The model's ordering — hold blocks disposition, and authorised erasure may reduce a tombstone — reflects the statutory exceptions for legal obligations, archiving and defence of legal claims, but the resolution is jurisdictional and must be decided by the adopting Dimension's records and privacy authorities, not by this model.

Verifiable-credential revocation semantics imply a status that can be flipped by the issuer at any time, whereas records doctrine requires the superseded state to remain retrievable. Resolved by treating credential status as a projection of the governed status, never as its master.

Access-to-documents regimes create a presumption of disclosure with enumerated exemptions, while security control catalogues start from deny-by-default. The model defaults to deny and treats proactive publication and statutory requests as recorded exceptions, which is conservative but will understate disclosure duties for public bodies unless the Dimension declares the access profile.

NARA's requirement set separates mandatory from preferred requirements for a records system, while this model states governance obligations for a decision record; an adopter should not read a 'Must Have' system requirement as satisfied merely because the corresponding governance field exists here.
regional_assumptions: The 40 CFR material is United States federal environmental review practice only, and is additionally superseded as described in the conflicts.
The Green Book and its multi-criteria supplement are HM Treasury guidance for United Kingdom central government and carry no authority elsewhere.
GDPR obligations on automated decision-making apply to processing within the EU and EEA scope; equivalent regimes in other jurisdictions are not assumed to impose the same content requirements.
NASA's decision analysis material is United States federal aerospace systems-engineering practice, used here as a method pattern rather than as a mandate.
No global default jurisdictional profile is asserted. An adopting Dimension must bind a profile per decision type, and an unbound decision type carries no profile-required content elements.
Language, locale and script of the decision question and outcome statement are recorded per decision; no single working language is assumed.

The duty to state reasons cited here is a Treaty obligation applying to EU legal acts; it is used as evidence that a stated reason is a governed object, not as a claim that private or non-EU decisions carry the same duty.

The right to explanation cited here applies to deployers of specified high-risk AI systems under EU law, with statutory exceptions; it does not establish a general right to explanation for all decisions in all jurisdictions.

OMB Circular A-4 is United States federal guidance for regulatory analysis, archived in the 2003 form consulted, and has been revised and contested since; it is cited as an illustrative public-authority requirement for sensitivity analysis and assumption transparency, not as a globally binding rule.

The certainty-of-evidence framework originates in health-evidence appraisal and is rendered here through a United States public-health handbook; transfer to engineering, legal or commercial decisions is by analogy and must be declared by the adopting Dimension.

Deliberative bodies differ in whether dissent is recorded, attributed or published at all; this model requires that dissent be preserved where it exists but does not assume any jurisdiction's disclosure rules.

Regulation (EC) No 1049/2001, Council Decision 2009/937/EU and Regulation (EU) 2016/679 are EU instruments used as profiles. They illustrate exemption grounds, partial access, quorum, proxy voting, written and silence procedures, storage limitation and erasure exceptions; they are not asserted to apply outside the EU.

NARA's Universal ERM Requirements and NIST SP 800-53 are United States federal profiles. Their requirement categories and control families inform structure but confer no obligation on non-US adopters.
ELI-style identifiers and Akoma Ntoso structures presume a legislative or deliberative context; for corporate or operational decisions they are optional alignments only.
No sources from Asia-Pacific, African, Latin American or Middle Eastern records or governance regimes were consulted in this pass, so region-specific duties there are unassessed.

The tiered appeal model drawn from RFC 2026 reflects one standards organisation's practice; statutory appeal rights, standing rules and time limits vary widely and must be supplied by the adopting Dimension.
adversarial_checks: Searched for a counterexample where a decision has no genuine alternatives, such as a mandatory statutory determination. The model accordingly permits an alternative set of size one plus an optional baseline, makes weights and aggregation optional, and never requires a ranking to exist for an outcome to be complete.

Tested whether DMN alone could carry the whole model. It cannot: the Decision element lacks alternatives, criteria, weights, rationale and disposition, and its identifier is document-scoped. DMN was therefore demoted to an alignment with a recorded conflict rather than adopted as a conformance target or an identity source.

Checked every finding and function against the two ledger relations and the six neighbouring models. Evidence appears only as a reference with a citation role, participants and approval appear only as an outbound reference, the carrying record appears only as a reference, and no function performs evaluation execution, enforcement or audit logging. The decision-rule finding was rewritten to record the rules relied upon plus a versioned source reference, with execution explicitly assigned to a decision service.

Tested whether the no-action requirement is universal. It is normative in the Green Book as the business-as-usual benchmark and was normative in the 2024 CFR edition of 40 CFR 1502.14, but is absent from DMN and from 42010. It is therefore modelled as a profile-conditional requirement with a recorded justification for absence, not as a globally mandatory field.

Checked the machine-gate conditions directly: identity priority names the authoritative master-system identifier first; the timestamp rule contains RFC 3339, seconds and offset and separates event from observation or ingestion time; the delete rules state tombstone, retention and erasure ownership; all local identifiers begin with dr-core-, are unique and contain no date-like component; every finding either declares artefacts with a null rationale or declares an empty artefact array with a substantive rationale, never both; question texts are distinct across the model and span eighteen distinct question kinds.

Probed whether the outcome finding smuggles in approval semantics. The disposition code names what the decision content states, and the function effects place approval execution, publication, filing and enforcement with the referenced models, so a consuming agent is instructed not to infer approval or legal effect from this model alone.

Checked every finding against the WM-KNW-008 reference rationale: no finding reproduces evidence identity, acquisition, custody, grading methodology or retention. The one finding that assesses evidence is explicitly scoped to a decision-local appraisal, carries the referenced certainty grade unchanged with a read time, and is inline-only so it cannot circulate as an evidence assessment report.

Tested whether the incoming WM-ACT-032 relation had leaked ownership: no bundle, layer, finding or function mentions change-request intake, triage, workflow or closure, and the composition entry states that this model only exposes resolvable identifiers.

Tested whether 'explainable decision trace' had become an audit trail. The trace finding, the rendition artefact and the access audit requirements all state that audit trails, access logging and disclosure approval belong to the `governance` split; the render function's effects say it is not an audit record and discharges no regulatory duty.

Tested whether the assumption and sensitivity function had become a runtime evaluator or enforcement engine. Its effects restrict it to annotating status and listing stale references, explicitly excluding executing analysis, re-running models, enforcing outcomes and changing decision state, with escalation left to governance.

Searched for the counterexample that argument standards imply an evaluation semantics. Assurance-case and argument-interchange sources describe auditable claims, arguments and evidence and asserted inference, not entailment computation, so the model records asserted inference and conflict and exposes no validity, soundness or acceptability function.

Checked that no structure asserts truth, legality or optimality: the policy layer forbids it, the render function's effects repeat it, and the causal finding is constrained to assertions with a strength qualifier and competing-explanation note rather than causal conclusions.

Rejected an attractive but unsupported structure: a 'rationale quality score' aggregating reason weights and evidence grades. No consulted primary source supports aggregation across those scales, so weighting is recorded as asserted values only and the aggregation question is logged as a gap.

Ownership sweep against the relation ledger: every bundle, layer, finding and function was re-read against the WM-ACT-032 and WM-KNW-008 rationales and against each outgoing reference. Approval execution, record disposal execution, evidence appraisal, claim structure, judicial reasoning, change-request lifecycle and rule evaluation were each found to be referenced only; where a draft concept drifted towards ownership — notably follow-up obligations and audit trails — it was reduced to an identifier-only reference and restated in out_of_scope or a boundary note.

Evaluation and enforcement test: the quorum function was deliberately renamed to attest rather than verify, and its effects state that no threshold computation or enforcement is performed. The integrity function verifies a digest but writes an outcome entry rather than acting on it, and the access layer emits classifications and instructions while enforcement is assigned to an external system.

Artefact collision test: the four artefacts introduced here (dr-gov-art-authority-register, dr-gov-art-lifecycle-ledger, dr-gov-art-access-schedule, dr-gov-art-disposition-record) were checked against the ten pre-existing core and reasoning artefact identifiers; none is re-created, renamed or shadowed, and dr-rsn-art-dissent-record is referenced by identifier only.

Identity falsifiability test: every artefact identity strategy and every local identifier was checked for date-derived or period-derived components. Serial names use a zero-padded sequence scoped to the decision master record, and the timestamp rule explicitly refuses bare dates, second-less times and offset-less times.

Exclusive representation test: each of the thirteen findings was checked to have either non-empty artefacts with a null rationale or an empty artefacts array with a substantive rationale; nine are inline-only with reasons that turn on reference-graph shape, personal-data minimisation or avoidance of duplicating an externally owned document.

Counterexample search for structure: a separate voting-record structure, a minutes artefact, an interests-register artefact and an implementation-tracking layer were each considered and rejected, because in every case an external owner already holds the concept and no primary source supported placing it here.
